thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: realtime-api p99 latency spike detected — p99=3.4s (SLO=1.5s) over last 3m. Affected: EU region. Dashboard: https://dash.internal/redwood/alerts/61677

alice (eng-oncall): I'm on it — grabbing dashboards and logs. paging SRE.

ben (sre): Looking now. Any indication of errors or increased traffic?

emily (support): We have two live chats reporting very slow responses from EU customers, both on chat flows. Not full failures, just high latency.

carla (eng-platform): Checking infra — KV cache metrics and pod-level latencies. Initial glance shows spike in kv_cache_miss_rate on eu-cluster-1.

ben (sre): Quick metrics snapshot: p95=850ms, p99=3.4s, req/s steady. error_rate=0.12%.

ben (sre): Node-level look: suspecting tail on node-gpu-7. Running quick pod checks:
```
kubectl get pods -n prod -l app=realtime-api -o wide
# realtime-api-7  Ready  1/1  node-gpu-7
kubectl logs realtime-api-7 --tail=100
# ... high KV cache miss log entries ...
```

carla (eng-platform): Confirmed: kv_miss_rate spiked ~00:54 UTC, correlated with a model cache eviction event. Looks like eviction policy kicked in during a small compaction job.

alice (eng-oncall): Mitigation: enable lower-latency model variant (quantized v2) for EU route and scale up realtime-api by +2 replicas. Executing fallback toggle now.

dave (eng-releases): Rolling canary toggles. Following runbook steps (latency-fallback v1) — tagging progress. If anyone needs the playbook: /playbooks/latency-fallback (internal).

incident-bot: Action logged — fallback_toggle executed by alice at 6167778894. Canary rolling to 5% -> 25% traffic.

frank (customer-success): Notified impacted customers and opened tickets CS-1298 and CS-1299. Customers notified that we're actively mitigating; no billing SLO breach yet reported.

ben (sre): After fallback + scale: p99 dropped to ~1.6s, p95 ~720ms. Still slightly above SLO but trending down. Continuing to watch KV hits and model load times.

emily (support): Sent customer update: "We're routing you to lower-latency model variant while we stabilize; continued updates in 15m."

alice (eng-oncall): Next steps: close immediate pager if stable, eng-platform to own root cause (cache eviction policy + compaction timing). @carla can you take post-incident ownership?

carla (eng-platform): Yep — I'll pull detailed metrics (kv cache hit/miss, cache size, eviction logs) and start a postmortem draft. Will include suggestions: stagger compactions, add eviction grace, and better pre-warm on deploy.

dave (eng-releases): Plan B (if regression): route-shift to dedicated capacity for EU and throttle background compactions. I'm sizing a quick reservation if needed.

incident-bot: Monitoring: p99 now 1.45s (< SLO). Will auto-close alert if remains < SLO for 15m.

alice (eng-oncall): Closing pager for now — system stabilizing. Monitoring for 30m then handoff to eng-platform for RCA. If p99 > 1.5s again, re-open. :white_check_mark:

ben (sre): I'll collect the tail latency traces and KV cache histograms and drop them in the postmortem thread.

frank (customer-success): I'll sync with the CS leads and attach customer-facing notes to the tickets.

carla (eng-platform): Drafting postmortem and timeline. Will create follow-up RFC for cache eviction policy.

incident-bot: Incident state: MITIGATED. Monitoring continuing until 6167779810.
